title: Was Christmas better in the past

vocabulary.meaning: the annual Christian holiday celebrated on 25 December and widely observed as a cultural festival
examples: Christmas traditions vary between families and countries.
Some people feel Christmas has changed over time.

vocabulary.meaning: a warm and sometimes sad feeling about the past
examples: Old Christmas songs can create nostalgia.
Nostalgia may make past celebrations seem better than they really were.

vocabulary.meaning: a custom passed from one generation to another
examples: Decorating a tree is a Christmas tradition in many homes.
Families often create their own traditions.
The town centre looked festive with lights and decorations.
People were in a festive mood.

vocabulary.meaning: the process of making something increasingly focused on selling and profit
examples: Some people criticise the commercialisation of Christmas.
Advertising contributes to holiday commercialisation.

vocabulary.meaning: the practice of giving presents to other people
examples: Gift-giving is an important part of many Christmas celebrations.
Some families set limits on gift-giving.

vocabulary.meaning: a meeting of relatives for a social occasion
examples: Christmas often involves a large family gathering.
Family gatherings can be joyful but sometimes stressful.

vocabulary.meaning: the period of life when someone is a child
examples: People often remember Christmas differently from their childhood.
Childhood memories can be especially powerful.

vocabulary.meaning: an enjoyable event marking a special occasion
examples: The celebration lasted all evening.
Different generations prefer different styles of celebration.

vocabulary.meaning: a traditional way of behaving or doing something
examples: Every country has its own seasonal customs.
The custom has continued for many years.
